issues: The printing ink initially contained metallic Ti and Nb plus ZrH2, HfH2, and TaH0.5; TiH2 and NbH formed during hydrogen treatment, so the initial-state description conflates processing stages.
The intervention omits pack-cementation silicide coating, a central manipulated step for oxidation resistance.
Water quenching from 1500 °C was applied only to selected homogenized samples for phase-transformation study, not as the standard continuation of sintering.
Oxygen was contamination rather than a controlled uptake, and hydride-driven oxygen scavenging was discussed but not directly established as the operative mechanism.
High-temperature mechanical tests used the stable slow-cooled multiphase material, not the quenched metastable single-BCC material.
The claimed baseline cracking and alpha-HCP embrittlement are not established; arc-melted material is described as metastable single BCC.
The paper does not establish that oxygen must be held near 1 wt.% or that any sintering time merely exceeding 15 min produces full densification; near-full density was obtained after 18 h.
